alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 2:34PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and moderate surf will cause moderate flooding in low lying
areas along the Redwood and Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.25 and 8.75
MLLW is expected at the Arena Cove tide gauge. At the Crescent
City tide gauge 9.5 to 10.0 feet MLLW is predicted.

* For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and
breaking waves of 25 to 30 feet are expected on Wednesday may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood and
Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 A
alerts.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

alerts.description:

astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Sal

alerts.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

key: Strong south wind will gradually build Monday and peak Tuesday with gusts over 45 mph ahead of a strong cold front.
Period of heavy rain along Tuesdays front with greatest rain focused in Mendocino County with 1 to 2 inches most likely. Additional rain later in the week.

High astronomical tides with water levels already increased by El Nino, will coincide with strong Pacific storm systems, likely generating record breaking Coastal Flooding Monday(11/23) through Thursday(11/26) at high tide. Greatest risk will be Tuesday and Wednesday.

- Mostly dry weather and near seasonable temperatures through Tuesday; Valley fog chances return overnight into Tuesday AM - Next weather system is trending weaker although rain, light high elevation mountain snow, and breezy southeast winds are still on track Tuesday PM - Wednesday AM - Return to dry and seasonable weather with additional Valley fog chances Thanksgiving Day into the early weekend

Updated at 1239 PM PST Mon Nov 23 2026 - Major to extreme coastal flooding this week - Impactful storm brings rain and gusty winds Tuesday evening into Wednesday morning - Drier conditions for Thanksgiving - Wet weather returns for the upcoming weekend

1. Dense fog advisory remains in effect through 11AM this morning for the San Joaquin Valley from Merced County to Delano. 2. Light rain and snow showers are possible Tuesday night into Wednesday morning with a low probability of any meaningful accumulation. 3. A ridge of high pressure will build back into our area through the Thanksgiving holiday.

Mild and dry conditions are expected into Tuesday except for some cold overnight temperatures. Light rain is possible again Tuesday night into Wednesday along the Central coast. Thanksgiving and Friday will be warm and dry. A cooling trend will begin over the weekend.

Dry conditions expected through Saturday. Today and Tuesday will see a few degrees of warming, Wednesday could see a minor cool down west of the mountains, before a more noticeable warm up for Thursday and Friday. Weak to locally moderate Santa Ana winds are expected for Thursday and Friday. Precipitation chances could return early next week, with low confidence in details. Widespread coastal flooding is expected this week due to King Tides and increased surf.
Cold temperatures and areas of freezing fog this morning, followed by mostly dry weather today through Tuesday afternoon.
A weak storm brings increased winds and light Sierra snow Tuesday night into Wednesday morning.
Dry and mild weather is favored for Thanksgiving Day, with additional storms possible late next weekend and beyond.
Breezy north winds are expected Wednesday and Thursday across the Colorado River Valley. This may result in hazardous boating conditions on large inland lakes.
A noted warming trend is expected the remainder of the week through the holiday weekend.
The next substantial storm system looks to impact the Western U.S. the first half of next week.

- Dry and mostly tranquil weather is expected to persist through at least the Thanksgiving Weekend. - Temperatures will embark on a gradual warming trend over the next several days as high pressure encompasses much of the western United Sates. - Periods of breezy conditions over high terrain areas and along the lower Colorado River Valley will be the only notable conditions to speak.
